facts.text: A cracked smartphone screen sends its owner looking for a repair shop.
People check directions on their phones instead of unfolding a paper road map.
A family group text helps relatives coordinate dinner and rides.
A phone battery running low leaves someone hunting for a charging cable.
People take photographs with their phones and share them almost immediately.
Many people unlock their phones with a passcode or fingerprint.
A shop customer compares prices online while standing in an aisle.
A cashier sometimes turns a small card terminal toward customers to enter a code.
A customer inserts a chip card into a payment terminal and waits for approval.
Some stores offer contactless payment by tapping a card or phone.
A restaurant offers free wireless internet and posts its password near the counter.
A slow wireless connection makes a video stop and buffer.
Many households stream television programs through an internet connection.
A family sometimes argues over which show to watch on a shared streaming account.
Some households keep cable television while others cancel it for online viewing.
Flat-screen televisions hang on walls or stand on narrow cabinets.
A game console downloads updates before a child can start playing.
A student types homework on a laptop and submits it through a school website.
Some schools lend students tablet or laptop computers for classroom work.
Office workers share documents through online storage instead of passing around disks.
A worker joins a video meeting using a laptop camera and headset.
A printer may connect to the household wireless network without a cable.
A household voice-controlled speaker can play music or answer simple questions.
A doorbell camera lets some homeowners see visitors on their phones.
A driver plugs a phone into the car to hear navigation instructions.
A customer waits for a delivery tracking page to show that a parcel has arrived.
A parent reminds a child to put down a tablet at the dinner table.
Some households use a small streaming device to show online videos on an older television.
